::: {.callout-tip}
### Goal of VS
**VS standardizes vital sign measurements** (e.g., BP, pulse, temperature, weight) into a consistent **Findings** structure so reviewers can **track values over time**, confirm **units/methods**, and validate **submission readiness**.
:::

## What VS is
**VS (Vital Signs)** is an SDTM **Findings** domain containing **vital sign test results** collected per subject, per timepoint/visit.
It supports longitudinal review by combining:
- a **test identifier** (`VSTESTCD` / `VSTEST`)
- a **result** (original + standardized)
- a **timing context** (datetime/visit/study day)
- optional **method/position/location** qualifiers

## What you’ll find here
- **Purpose:** Tabulate vital signs in a reviewable, time-ordered structure
- **Traceability:** Source/EDC vitals forms → VS → ADaM (e.g., ADVS) → TLFs (shift tables/plots, outliers)
- **Typical tests:** SBP/DBP, pulse, temperature, respiratory rate, height/weight (and sometimes BMI)

---

## Core structure (Findings pattern)

### Keys you’ll see everywhere
VS follows standard SDTM keys:
- `STUDYID` — Study identifier  
- `DOMAIN` — Always `"VS"`  
- `USUBJID` — Unique subject identifier  
- `VSSEQ` — Record sequence

### Test identification
- `VSTESTCD` — Short test code (e.g., `SYSBP`, `DIABP`, `PULSE`, `TEMP`)
- `VSTEST` — Decoded test name (e.g., “Systolic Blood Pressure”)

### Results (original vs standardized)
- `VSORRES` / `VSORRESU` — Original result + unit (as collected)
- `VSSTRESC` / `VSSTRESN` — Standardized result (char / numeric)
- `VSSTRESU` — Standardized unit

::: {.callout-note}
### Units matter in VS
If sites collect in mixed units (e.g., °F and °C), **preserve the original** (`VSORRES/VSORRESU`) and provide a **consistent standardized** unit (`VSSTRESN/VSSTRESU`) with documented conversion rules.
:::

---

## Timing & visit context

VS typically includes one or more of:
- **ISO datetime:** `VSDTC` (character ISO 8601)
- **Study day:** `VSDY` (numeric study day)
- **Visit:** `VISIT`, `VISITNUM`
- Optional timepoint variables when applicable (e.g., `VSTPT`, `VSTPTNUM`, `VSELTM`)

---

## Common qualifiers (how/where collected)
Depending on your CRF and protocol:
- `VSPOS` — Position (e.g., SITTING, SUPINE)
- `VSLOC` — Location (e.g., ARM, ORAL)
- `VSMETHOD` — Method/device (when collected)
- `VSCAT` / `VSSCAT` — Category/subcategory (helpful for grouping panels)

---

## Mini examples

### Example 1 — Blood pressure + pulse at Baseline
| USUBJID | VSSEQ | VSTESTCD | VSTEST | VSORRES | VSORRESU | VSSTRESN | VSSTRESU | VSPOS | VISIT | VSDTC |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| ABC123-001-1001 | 1 | SYSBP | Systolic Blood Pressure | 128 | mmHg | 128 | mmHg | SITTING | Baseline | 2025-01-15T09:12 |
| ABC123-001-1001 | 2 | DIABP | Diastolic Blood Pressure | 82 | mmHg | 82 | mmHg | SITTING | Baseline | 2025-01-15T09:12 |
| ABC123-001-1001 | 3 | PULSE | Pulse Rate | 74 | bpm | 74 | bpm | SITTING | Baseline | 2025-01-15T09:12 |

### Example 2 — Temperature in original °F, standardized to °C
| USUBJID | VSSEQ | VSTESTCD | VSTEST | VSORRES | VSORRESU | VSSTRESN | VSSTRESU | VSLOC | VISIT | VSDTC |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| ABC123-001-1001 | 10 | TEMP | Temperature | 98.6 | F | 37.0 | C | ORAL | Week 2 | 2025-01-29T10:05 |

## Traceability map (review-friendly)
A typical traceability chain:
**Source/EDC vitals page → VS (tabulation) → ADVS (analysis-ready) → TLFs**

**Example**
- Vitals CRF → **VS** (`VSTESTCD/VSDTC/VSORRES/VSSTRESN/...`) → **ADVS** (baseline flags, analysis visits/windows) → shift tables, time profiles, outlier listings

**Proof points**
- **Source → VS:** aCRF annotations + define.xml origins
- **VS → ADVS:** define.xml MethodDefs + ADRG derivations (baseline rules, visit windows)

---

## Common QC checks (VS)
- `USUBJID + VSSEQ` unique; domain keys populated
- `VSTESTCD` ↔ `VSTEST` consistent (no mismatches)
- Original vs standardized results aligned (conversion rules correct)
- Units present and valid; no “unit drift” within a test
- Timing present and consistent (`VSDTC`, `VISIT/VISITNUM`, `VSDY`)
- Position/location/method populated when required by protocol
- Out-of-range or implausible values flagged for review (medical review consistency)

---

## Best practices
- Standardize to **one canonical unit** per vital sign in `VSSTRESU`
- Preserve **as-collected** values in `VSORRES/VSORRESU` (do not overwrite)
- Keep datetime rules consistent (partial/missing handling documented)
- Use qualifiers (`VSPOS`, `VSLOC`, `VSMETHOD`) to prevent mixing non-comparable measurements
- Treat VS as **review-first**: sorted, clean, and easy to trend over time
